text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/donor-design-sol.md <<'EOF'
# Individual donor name design sketch

## Caller and contract

Keep `FunderNameFeatures::from_name(Option<&str>)` as the only public construction boundary. Callers still supply source evidence once. The result adds `person_titles: Vec<PersonTitle>` and `person_name_normalized: Option<String>`. A source `Lord (Michael) Farmer` retains exact `name_raw`, existing `name_normalized = "lord (michael) farmer"`, and `parenthetical_text = ["Michael"]`; new fields contain `[Lord]` and `"michael farmer"`. A reconstructed titled comparison rendering is `"lord michael farmer"`. If a case-preserving rendering is actually requested, add a separately named display representation rather than changing the documented lowercase meaning of normalized.

`person_core` stays the punctuation-normalized title-free comparison representation. Derive it and `person_initials` from the same single title decomposition as the new representation. No first-name or surname fields. Word boundaries do not prove those roles, and compound surnames remain intact.

## Minimal typed shape

In `funder_name.rs`, define one canonical `PersonTitle` enum for the existing recognized vocabulary. Give it a single token parser and canonical serialization spelling. Retain the existing set, including mr, mrs, ms, miss, mx, dr, prof, professor, sir, dame, lord, lady, rev, reverend, rt, hon. Preserve the distinction between prof and professor unless explicit canonicalization is wanted. Parser accepts case-insensitive NFKC input and an optional trailing period. Titles are recognized only as a contiguous leading sequence, never globally.

Use a private `PersonNameParts { titles: Vec<PersonTitle>, normalized: String }` with a single private parsing function that owns leading-title extraction and conservative parentheses handling. Expose no independent parser options or public staged methods. Missing and withheld names have no person representation and empty titles. A title-only input has empty titles or recognized titles according to an explicitly documented convention, but `person_name_normalized` must be None, never Some(""). Prefer retaining recognized titles with absent remaining name as parallel evidence.

These are candidate person features, matching the module's existing parallel-feature model. They do not assert that a funder is an individual. Organisation fields and classification remain unchanged. An organisation starting with Lord can have person candidate features without changing its organisation identity.

## Parentheses rule

Only unwrap a balanced, nonnested parenthetical group immediately after recognized leading titles, with nonempty name-like contents and a nonempty trailing name-like sequence. The target is `Lord (Michael) Farmer`. Require alphabetic name tokens with ordinary name punctuation such as apostrophes or hyphens; refuse digits, commas, conjunctions, role descriptions, alias markers, nested groups and unmatched parentheses. Keep the original evidence in all cases. Do not globally remove parentheses from `name_normalized`, primary organisation names, acronym evidence, or aliases. `BJD (GB) Limited`, `HSBC UK (Ian Stuart, CEO)`, and `Lord Smith (trustee)` must preserve their existing source-level representations. The exact allowlist of name punctuation is a local parser policy, not another title vocabulary.

The existing `person_core` already removes punctuation from all parenthetical text. Do not broaden that behavior accidentally while adding the new conservative person representation. Build its title stripping from the canonical enum; derive core from the appropriate existing token sequence if preserving its outputs is necessary.

## Producer and consumer trace

1. `declaration_cleaning.rs` domain `FunderObservation::new` currently calls `FunderNameFeatures::from_name` for donor, payer and ultimate-payer observations. Keep that construction path. `FunderObservation` flattens the features through Serde, so both additive fields automatically reach serialized records.
2. `outbound/declaration_cleaning.rs::funders_schema` must add nullable UTF8 `person_name_normalized` and nonnullable list-of-UTF8 `person_titles`. Its explicit Arrow schema controls JSON-to-Arrow publication; Serialize alone does not persist new fields.
3. `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs` reads `funders.parquet` against the full `funders_schema`. Its required-field check means the additive schema will reject older cleaned artifacts. Keep the existing explicit recapture/clean/resolve/load message, or deliberately introduce a versioned reader if old-artifact compatibility is a real requirement. Do not pretend Serde defaults alone solve Arrow schema compatibility.
4. `declaration_resolution/input.rs::Observation` currently reads name_raw, name_normalized, organisation_core and aliases, and ignores person_core/person_initials. New person fields can remain ignored by this consumer in this scoped cleaning improvement. Scoring rows, blocking keys, exact-name matching, alias matching and preferred names currently use name_normalized. Leave those semantics unchanged unless the user expressly intends identity resolution to change.
5. If resolution should use the new person representation, that is a separate cohesive change through Observation, donor-kind gating, blocking, scorer rows, pair evidence and identity output. Do not silently swap all `name_normalized` consumers. `identity.rs` exact-name and raw-name trade-union/organisation logic must keep original meaning.
6. Loading and public funder APIs consume resolved identities, not these feature columns. No SQL migration, frontend change or public financial semantic change is needed for additive cleaning evidence.

## Structurally distinct alternative

Replace the parallel top-level fields with `person: Option<PersonNameFeatures>` and serialize it as a nullable Arrow struct containing titles, normalized name, core and initials. This makes related person features cohesive and impossible to confuse with organisation fields, and permits an explicit parse outcome type later. It requires changing existing flattened person_core/person_initials columns, Arrow schema shape, all fixture expectations and any offline consumers. Keeping old top-level columns alongside the struct would create two writable representations. For this narrow request, the additive flat design hides parsing behind the existing single boundary and avoids an unnecessary artifact migration. Prefer it, with the private cohesive struct internally.

## Verification and red-flag screen

Unit cases cover Mr/Mrs/Lord/Dame, trailing periods, multiple titles, plain names, apostrophes, compound surnames, internal title words, no name, placeholders, title-only values, balanced target parentheses, nested/unbalanced groups and organisation examples. Assert raw source, generic normalized name and organisation features remain stable. Confirm exact target fields rather than only title removal.

Extend `exposed/tests/declaration_cleaning.rs` with real captured declaration fixtures and read the emitted `funders.parquet`. Assert actual Arrow list/nullability/types and row values for an individual donor and organisation; ensure a resolution read succeeds for the new artifact. This proves the explicit schema did not silently discard fields. Existing resolution fixtures should remain valid because comparison semantics are unchanged, but old physical cleaned artifacts require regeneration under the existing strict reader.

The canonical enum removes the existing hand-synced-title risk. The one private parse operation avoids shallow public methods and split ownership. No metadata is inferred beyond a syntactic person candidate. The alternative nested artifact has stronger cohesion but worse compatibility and interface cost for this request.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

Saved design sketch to `/tmp/donor-design-sol.md`.

Recommend additive `person_titles` and `person_name_normalized`, owned by the existing construction boundary, with one canonical title enum. Preserve raw and organisation representations. Handle parentheses conservatively.

Critical integration finding: adding Arrow fields makes existing cleaned artifacts fail resolution’s required-schema check. Serde defaults alone cannot provide compatibility.

The sketch includes a nested-struct alternative, producer/consumer tracing, and real Parquet verification cases.
